faq.question: Why choose CJC-1295 without DAC?
faq.answer: Choice depends on research objective. No DAC = ~30 min half-life = discrete physiological GH pulse. With DAC = ~8 day half-life = sustained GH/IGF-1 elevation. Use no DAC for pulsatile GH studies; use DAC for chronic activation.

faq.question: Is CJC-1295 (no DAC) the same as Mod GRF 1-29?
faq.answer: Essentially yes. Both refer to the same 30-amino acid GHRH analogue with four substitutions but without the DAC linker. Both terms describe the short-acting, non-albumin-binding variant.

faq.question: What is the optimal partner peptide?
faq.answer: Ipamorelin is preferred for pulsatile protocols: CJC-1295 provides GHRH signal, Ipamorelin suppresses somatostatin tone → synergistic, clean GH pulse. GHRP-2 can be used when maximum pulse amplitude is preferred over selectivity.

faq.question: What is the half-life difference vs DAC variant?
faq.answer: No DAC: ~30 minutes → discrete GH pulse. With DAC: ~8 days (via albumin conjugation). This ~400-fold difference is entirely due to the maleimidopropionyl DAC linker.

faq.question: How is absence of DAC verified?
faq.answer: HPLC-MS confirms the molecular ion without the maleimidopropionyl mass adduct (+97 Da absent vs DAC variant). Included in every batch-specific COA.
